decisions.quote: We failed to replicate Napier and Jost’s finding that system-justifying ideology mediated the relationship between conservatism and life satisfaction.
decisions.reason: The abstract explicitly states that the study failed to replicate Napier and Jost's mediation finding, which is the specific finding attributed to the original paper and the central claim tested against the authors' alternative explanation.

Is conservatism-life-satisfaction association itself a tested original finding satisfying implicit comparison criteria, giving mixed, or merely background/preliminary premise around the central original mediation claim, giving failed? Explicit failure of one mediation is not automatically overall verdict on all original findings under Rule1. blind_target.authors: Napier J. N., Jost J. T.
blind_target.title: Why are conservatives happier than liberals?
blind_target.evidence_quote: We failed to replicate Napier and Jost’s finding that system-justifying ideology mediated the relationship between conservatism and life satisfaction.
blind_target.outcome_quote: In a study ( N = 816), we find that conservatives are more satisfied with life than liberals and that conservatism is associated with higher socioeconomic status (SES). Taking SES as a starting point, we find that those with high SES have access to more group memberships and that this is associated with higher life satisfaction. We failed to replicate Napier and Jost’s finding that system-justifying ideology mediated the relationship between conservatism and life satisfaction.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: Abstract confirms the conservatism–happiness association but explicitly fails the proposed mediation; no overall verdict about both findings is available. Citation copied from publisher reference listing, with its printed initials retained.
